objectClass.notes: Static monumental landmark building, exterior shell only. No interior geometry: a prop kit is only ever looked at from outside, so an interior costs draw calls, geometries and VRAM for something nobody sees. Nothing moves, so one root pivot and zero sockets is the correct contract. The developer-built white condo of the last fifteen years: a six-storey white render box with a deep white coping cap, dark vertical fins and two vertical louvre boxes dividing six bays, glass-balustrade balconies in bays B, C and E and grid windows in A, D and F on every floor, a taller glazed ground floor with a white-framed lobby portal under a flat canopy on two stainless posts, a BAAN JAI CONDO board, planters with a hedge and fan palms, and a timber batten screen enclosing a roof deck with a lift head inside it.

reasoning: The silhouette is a white box under a coping cap, and the identity is the RHYTHM across it: dark vertical fins and two louvre boxes dividing six bays, three of which are recessed balconies with frosted balustrades and three grid windows, on every one of five floors.

The roof carries a 3.15 m timber batten screen over most of the deck with a lift head inside it -- the second identity feature, read from the elevated plate and placed against it, not against the proxy, which pushed it to the rear 40 percent of the roof.
The -X flank has its own grammar: a rear wall, a pair of dark louvre boxes with a glazed gap and white ledges between them, a strip of narrow windows, and a plain front wall.
Action readiness is minimal: static exterior shell, box collider, not breakable.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Thirty bays at four or five parts each plus 30 side panes, 580 screen battens and 132 louvre slats are over a thousand discrete parts; seven InstancedMesh systems carry all of them at one submission each, three of them scaling ONE unit box per instance (every pane, mullion, rail and fin body), so the whole prop is 13 draw calls.

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 21.80 x 21.00 x 17.30 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=32000 triangles, <=24 draw calls, <=16 materials, <=32 unique geometries.
Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot and zero sockets; box collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

silhouette.description: A 20.5 x 14.0 m body from the ground to a 17.75 m roof slab under a 1.1 m coping cap standing 0.35 m proud (17.4..18.5); fins and louvre boxes 0.3..0.6 m proud of the +Z and -Z faces, louvre boxes 0.67 m proud of the flanks; a 3.15 m batten screen over the deck to 21.0 with a lift head to 20.7 inside it; a canopy 2.5 m out at 2.4..2.6 and 0.5 m planters 1.2 m out at the base. The silhouette events are the coping cap, the screen, the fin returns and the canopy.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: Height is the primary axis at the declared 21.00 m: the top rail of the roof screen. The Meshy v7 proxy of the plate normalises to w:h:d = 1.036 : 1 : 0.842, so the bounding box is 21.8 x 21.0 x 17.7; on its +Z depth map at 47.06 px/m the BODY reads 965 px = 20.5 m wide and on the -X map 13.95 m deep, the side louvre boxes 0.65 m proud on each flank (21.8) and the canopy 2.1 m in front. The list-time 24 x 16 was a six-bay-at-4 m estimate: the proxy and the plate agree on six bays of 2.5 m between 0.3 m fins, two 1.85 m louvre boxes and 0.45 m corner fins (0.9 + 15.0 + 0.9 + 3.7 = 20.5), and the declaration was corrected on the asset with this arithmetic before the build. Built box: x -10.92..10.92 (side louvre slats), y 0..21.0, z -7.72 (rear louvre slats, mirrored from the front) ..+9.6 (entrance paving under the 2.5 m canopy) = 17.32, declared 17.3. Origin base-center of the BODY footprint, so the box is 0.94 m off-centre in z.
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: Independent Meshy v7 reconstruction of the same plate normalises to w:h:d = 1.036 : 1 : 0.842 against the corrected declaration 1.038 : 1 : 0.824. Area-weighted band comparison over ten bands: mean |delta width| 0.031 and |delta depth| 0.030 of height. Three residuals are explained rather than built to: (1) bands 2-7 width +0.042, where the candidate 95th percentile lands on the flank louvre bodies at x=10.75 and the proxy's on its wall at 10.25 -- the two bounding boxes agree (21.84 vs 21.76); (2) band 9 depth +0.149, the roof screen, which the proxy places on the rear 40 percent of the roof (front run 7.7 m behind the facade) and the plate does not: the plate shows the front run's full base with a 13 px deck strip in front of it at 39 px/m, where the proxy's placement would show ~80 px, and the lift head directly behind that run seen through the battens; (3) band 1 depth -0.081, a 5-95 percentile artefact of a thin canopy (28 m2 in a 300 m2 band) that the proxy fused with the planting. Floor pitch 2.85 m and ground floor 3.05 m from the proxy's slab lines at y 165/300/435/570/700/835 px.

AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Make material and form readable under neutral turntable lighting plus optional reference lighting.

AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the hero4x class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

drawCalls.note: Six components and seven repetition systems: 13 of 24. Three of the systems scale ONE unit box per instance, which is what lets every pane, every mullion and every fin body ride one draw each regardless of size.

materials.note: white covers every rendered surface; alu covers the mullions AND the fin bodies; eleven of sixteen, two of them (plant, sign) white bases carrying per-instance tints or a canvas.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 18844 of 32,000. The battens are 6,960 of it (580 x 12) and the mullion instances 3,984; the facade extrusions with thirty holes each are ~2,500 and the shrubs 1,600. Instancing means the battens upload once.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: Extrusions with holes for the facades and flanks, an extrusion in the YZ plane for the side walls, a notched plan extrusion for the ground floor, a plan ring for the coping, boxes, an icosahedron for the shrubs. The bay openings are holes in a Shape, not panels applied, so the reveals are real and the shell has no interior coincidence.
Seven InstancedMesh systems carry 1,185 of the prop's 1,191 discrete parts: 580 battens, 332 aluminium parts and fin bodies, 85 panes, 132 slats, 30 balustrades, 20 shrubs, 6 palms.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.

Every material is declared textureless. Two post-construction canvases are assigned in the browser only: the BAAN JAI / CONDO lettering and the curtain-and-reflection stripes on the shared glass -- the documented printed-graphic route, neither the five-canvas procedural set. Under Node the sign is its pale ground and the glass flat.
